boxes.text: This number box is connected to the pattrstorage object through the pattr object.
Open the storagewindow to see this patcher's pattr system and stored presets (slots).
Set number box to a value.
Change values (step 2), then store new values in preset 2.
Open Slot Storage window and delete all presets.
Fills a menu object with slotnames so that the menu's Item Number can be used to recall presets.
Output list of slotnames for all presets, with "undefined" slotnames for unused preset numbers, if any, between presets…
…or output list of slotnames for stored presets (same message, but with non-zero argument).
Each preset can have a slotname. Although slotnames can't be used to store and recall presets, they stay with the data, even if the preset number is changed.
Shift-click to store a preset in the  pattrstorage named "interface". Click to recall.
The preset object's pattrstorage attribute is set to the name of the pattrstorage it controls.
The preset object can be used to store and recall pattrstorage presets.
Output a list of all presets (slots)
Delete preset 1 and decrement higher-numbered presets by 1.
Delete preset 2 and do not renumber.
Open Storage Slots window with all presets cleared.
Presets can be rearranged and copied after their data is stored.
Move chord stored in preset 1 to preset 2, then store new chord in preset 1.
When greedy = 0 (default) pattrstorage objects in subpatchers block their UI-objects from this pattrstorage.
recall a single parameter from this preset.
recall a single parameter from this preset, sending the name and value out pattrstorage's outlet.
store a single parameter to this preset, if the preset already exists.
store a single parameter to this preset, creating new presets if necessary.
enable/disable preset recall for all UI-object inside patcher.
This patcher's pattrstorage stores the data of objects inside this subpatcher…
enable/disable preset recall for UI-object inside patcher.
Individual pattr objects and/or subpatchers can be stored/recalled/enabled/disabled.

If pattrstorage's name (its scripting name) is not explicitly given (as an argument or attribute), Max will generate a unique name that looks something like u000000000. Look in the Inspector, at Scripting Name.
pattrstorage will load storage.json if it is in the Max search path, but will not try to save changes.
The savemode attribute determines how pattrstorage will react when the patch is saved or closed after parameters have  changed.
read <filename>: write pattrstorage data from disk
read and write, using the same file that was last used.
write <filename>: write pattrstorage data to disk
The contents of pattrstorage can be saved to disk and will be recalled when the patch is loaded.
Interpolated data can result in unnecessary processing. When changemode = 1, only changed data output.
This table implements a "sticky middle" interpolation. Note that the table itself should not be included in this pattr system.
Threshhold: switches to second preset below 0.74
Select another type of interpolation and repeat step 4.
Threshhold: switches to second preset above 0.74
Move the points (step 1), then store new values in preset 3.
Set the four points on this function.
Tortoise's pattr values are still recalled before hare's, but hubris is restored first within each subpatcher.
Since 0 is less than 1, tortoise's pattr values are still recalled before hare's.
This patcher's pattrstorage stores the data of objects inside these two subpatchers.
The tortoise patcher has priority -1, which means its pattr values are recalled before the hare's, because the hare has priority 1.
Set hubris to be restored before speed in both hare and tortoise.
Edit priority in the client window, making tortoise priority 0.

pattrstorage client objects are grouped according to priority. Clients with smaller priority values are recalled before clients with larger priority values. This is useful when parts of the patch must be updated before other parts are.

Paste the patch below into a Max for Live device, then store a preset in the pattrstorage and save the device. The resulting preset will be embedded in the device, so there's no need to save the presets as a separate external file.
In Max for Live, if you set the parameter_enable attribute (Parameter Mode Enable = 1) and Initial Enable of a pattrstorage object, it will visible to the Live set as a Blob parameter.
A small pattr system for this help patch.
